# Review panel 1a: one runReview() for engine and eval, finding schema v2

Part of #117; replaces half of #125. **Behaviour must stay identical to today.**

1. **One review entry point.** Move the review stage's model work out of `src/pipeline/engine.ts` into `runReview(deps, input)` in `src/pipeline/review.ts`. That covers building the prompt, the invocation, parsing, the derived verdict, and blocking vs follow-up findings. The engine calls it, and the review eval's first-round path calls it (`src/evals/prepare.ts` / runner). `deps` supplies the invoker, so tests use the fake harness.
2. **Finding schema v2.** Review findings gain `failure_scenario` (string), `category` (one of correctness, security, reliability, data, concurrency, compatibility, test-gap, cleanup, conventions), `confidence` (number) and `introduced_by_diff` (boolean).
   - They're required in the model output schemas and requested in the prompt.
   - `toStrictJsonSchema` strips numeric bounds by design, for provider strict-mode compatibility. So **clamp `confidence` into [0,1] at parse time**. Don't try to put bounds in the JSON schema.
   - Stored and persisted types keep these fields optional, so reviews recorded before this change (run state, `review-N.json`, eval trials) still load, replay and regrade.

- later-round (previous-findings) eval cases;

# UI: inactive artifact tabs on the run page are barely legible

On the run page's artifacts panel, the inactive tabs (e.g. `spec.md`, `diff.patch`, `review-0.json`) render as light-grey boxes with dark-grey text and are almost unreadable.

**Cause.** `.tab` (in `ui/styles.css`, "artifacts" section) is applied to a `<button>` (`ui/components/ArtifactsPanel.tsx`), but it never resets the button's user-agent styles. Inactive tabs get the browser's default grey button background, and the text colour `--text-faint` (#56666f) sits on top of it. Only `.tab.active` sets its own background, which is why the active tab looks fine.

**Fix** (CSS only, in the existing token system):
- `.tab`: `background: transparent`, `appearance: none`, and inherit font and line height; keep the mono font.
- Inactive tab text uses `--text-dim` (#94a6b2): about 8:1 contrast on `--bg`, and it meets WCAG AA.
- `.tab:hover` keeps `--text` and gets a subtle `--bg-hover` background.
- `.tab.active` is unchanged.
- Add a visible `:focus-visible` outline, using `--accent`, for keyboard users.

Check that no other `.tab` usage elsewhere in the UI regresses: grep for `class="tab"`.

OpenRouter spend reconciliation

Today the OpenRouter budget (limits.openrouter_budget_usd, default $50) is enforced only on locally
estimated spend (token counts × catalog price, rolling 30 days, see ProviderTracker.headroom and
Store.providerSpendSince). Reconcile it against OpenRouter's own numbers.

- Poll `GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/key` (Bearer OPENROUTER_API_KEY) every 10 minutes while the
  provider is enabled, and before a metered OpenRouter invocation when the last reading is older than
  2 minutes. The response is `{ data: { usage, usage_daily, usage_weekly, usage_monthly, limit,
  limit_remaining, limit_reset, ... } }` (USD). Note `limit` resets on `limit_reset` (currently
  "daily" on our key), so `limit_remaining` is NOT the budget; the configured budget is.
- Budget enforcement uses the larger of the local 30-day estimate and `usage_monthly` (fail safe:
  never let a missing or failed reading loosen the budget; treat `limit_remaining <= 0` as exhausted
  until the next reading).
- Surface `reportedUsageUsd` (monthly), `reportedAt`, and the key's `limit`/`limitRemaining`/
  `limitReset` on the OpenRouter entry of `/api/providers` and in the UI provider card; show
  "estimated vs reported" spend.
- Drift check: when the reported usage delta since the previous reading differs from the locally
  recorded cost of OpenRouter invocations in the same interval by more than 20% (and more than
  $0.05 absolute), write a warn event with both numbers.
- Never log or expose the key or the `label` field.
- Tests with an injected fetch and fake clock: budget uses the larger number, failed readings don't
  loosen it, drift warning fires only above both thresholds, polling interval respected.

# Conflict-free migrations for parallel branches

## Why
`src/db/migrations.ts` is one array with sequential `version` integers. Two parallel runs that each add a migration both append `version: N+1` at the end of the same array, so every such pair conflicts, and the orchestrator has renumbered by hand several times (v5–v12).

## Design
- One file per new migration: `src/db/migrations/<UTC timestamp>-<slug>.sql`, e.g. `20260927T1500-run-dependencies.sql`. Files load at startup (`readdirSync`, sorted by filename) and are applied in order inside a transaction each.
- Track applied migrations by name in a `schema_migrations(name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, applied_at INTEGER)` table. On first start after this change, record the existing array migrations 1..N (named `legacy-0001-<name>`...) as applied according to the current `user_version`. The legacy array stays frozen and append-only rules move to the directory.
- The directory must never contain two files with the same name; tests fail if a file is edited after it ships (keep a checked-in hash list, `src/db/migrations/SHIPPED`, which the test compares).
- Update AGENTS.md: "New persisted fields need a new file in `src/db/migrations/`".

## Acceptance
- Tests:
  - a fresh DB applies legacy plus directory migrations;
  - an existing DB at `user_version = N` applies only new files;
  - two files added on different branches apply in filename order regardless of merge order;
  - an edited shipped file fails the test.
- Starting the daemon on a copy of the production DB is a no-op except the new table. The orchestrator verifies this before deploy.
- `bun run check` passes; under ~300 lines.

# Concurrency limits from config, and parallel slots for local models

## Why
Provider concurrency (`claude` 3, `codex` 3, `openrouter` 4, local 1) is hard-coded in the catalog, and `max_concurrent_runs` defaults to 3. The owner has plenty of subscription capacity, so these limits (not quota) cap throughput. Local servers may also sustain more than one request with batched decoding.

## Design
- `[providers.<id>] max_concurrent = N` in config.toml overrides `ProviderDef.maxConcurrent`, validated as a positive integer. Unknown provider ids are a config error. `limitless providers` shows the effective limit.
- Keep the defaults unchanged in code. The owner's config raises them.
- **Operations (orchestrator, not the run):**
  - Benchmark twilight's llama-server with `--parallel 2` (context split per slot) against 1: aggregate tokens/s and per-request latency on a review-sized prompt. Adopt 2 slots if aggregate throughput improves by at least 30% without per-request context dropping below what review needs.
  - Check whether mtplx can serve concurrent requests.
  - Record results in docs/research.

## Acceptance
- Config parsing tests: override applied, invalid value rejected, unknown provider rejected. The tracker uses the effective limit.
- `bun run check` passes; under ~150 lines.
